title: The Seventeenth Arrondissement and Back: Deleuze, the Lung, and the Seminar at Vincennes
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Paris, 17th arrondissement: the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested; full date given by both the English and French Wikipedia articles
stops.campa: In the 17th arrondissement a son is born to Louis Deleuze, an engineer and veteran of the first war, and to Odette Camauer. The household is comfortable and conservative. No source names the building; the arrondissement is the whole of the record. An older brother, Georges, is already there. Seventy years on the philosopher will go out of a window three quarters of a mile from this point, in the same district. The two ends of the life stand twenty minutes apart on foot.
suggested_refs: Birth registers of the 17th arrondissement, January 1925, for the unnamed address

stops.name: Lycee Carnot, boulevard Malesherbes: the classmate Guy Moquet
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; attendance at Carnot is attested but no source gives a year, and the Moquet overlap forces a pre-1940 period. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: On the boulevard Malesherbes the boy attends the Lycee Carnot. Guy Moquet is in the same school; Moquet is arrested in October 1940 and shot as a hostage at Chateaubriant a year later, aged seventeen, and his farewell letter will be read aloud in French classrooms for sixty years. Pierre Vial teaches him. In the neighbouring preparatory classes Maurice Merleau-Ponty holds a post, not yet anybody's master here. The classmate detail only works if the Carnot years begin before the Germans reach Paris.
suggested_refs: Enrolment records of the Lycee Carnot, 145 boulevard Malesherbes, for the classes of 1938-1940

stops.name: Deauville: the year in Normandy
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 1940-1941; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: The Germans take Paris and the family sends the boy to be schooled in Normandy, at Deauville, for a year. A teacher there turns him toward literature for the first time. The French account names Pierre Halbwachs; the Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy names Pierre Vial at Carnot the year before, and the two do not agree on who did it or where. The year that opens him to books is the year the country is occupied, and he spends it away from the city he will otherwise almost never leave.
suggested_refs: School records at Deauville for the year 1940-1941, and the teaching post of Pierre Halbwachs

stops.name: Drancy, the Cite de la Muette: the transit camp
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; no source checked names Drancy in Georges Deleuze's case, and no source gives a year for the arrest. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: At the Cite de la Muette in Drancy, a half-built housing estate turned transit camp, the convoys of the Paris region are assembled before they leave for the east. Georges Deleuze, arrested by the Germans for Resistance work, is deported. No source checked places him here; the stop rests on the standard routing of the period and on nothing else. Gilles is a schoolboy. He will speak of his brother almost never, and the household will carry the loss as the thing not discussed.
suggested_refs: The Drancy convoy lists held at the Memorial de la Shoah, checked for the name Deleuze

stops.name: Auschwitz-Birkenau: the brother who does not arrive
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; every source checked reports the death without a year, and the 1944 date is an inference, not a record
stops.campa: Georges Deleuze dies during the deportation. The English Wikipedia, the Stanford Encyclopedia and the Internet Encyclopedia all say he died on the train to Auschwitz; the French page for the Lycee Carnot lists a Deleuze among its alumni as a resistant who died in a camp. The two accounts differ on whether he reached the place at all, and neither gives a year. Georges had been the family's promising son, the one who acted. Gilles is the one left in the flat.
suggested_refs: Deportation records for Georges Deleuze, to settle whether he died in transit or in the camp

stops.name: Lycee Louis-le-Grand: hypokhagne and khagne
stops.date_confidence: contested; the French record puts the khagne at Louis-le-Grand, the Stanford and Internet encyclopedias put it at Henri IV. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: After the Liberation he does hypokhagne and khagne in the rue Saint-Jacques, at Louis-le-Grand, according to the French record. The Stanford Encyclopedia and the Internet Encyclopedia both put the khagne at Henri IV instead, and no tiebreaker has been found. The two schools stand four hundred metres apart on the same hill, which is how a contradiction of this kind survives seventy years. He is twenty. These are the last years anyone will grade him against a syllabus.
suggested_refs: Class lists of the khagne at Louis-le-Grand and at Henri IV for 1944-1946, to adjudicate the conflict

stops.name: Lycee Henri-IV, rue Clovis: Jean Beaufret's course
stops.date_confidence: attested by the French record for the period, without a precise date; month and day inferred
stops.campa: Alongside his own school he crosses the Montagne Sainte-Genevieve to sit in on Jean Beaufret's courses at the Lycee Henri-IV. Beaufret is the man through whom the Heideggerian current reaches a generation of French students, and Deleuze takes it at the source. He will then spend a working life building a philosophy of difference that owes the question of Being almost nothing at all. He leaves the rue Clovis with a vocabulary he declines to use, and with the habit of attending lectures he is not enrolled in.
suggested_refs: Beaufret's teaching notes at Henri-IV in the immediate postwar years

stops.name: The Sorbonne: the history of philosophy, and the agregation
stops.date_confidence: attested for the span 1944-1948; the pin is placed at October 1945, inside the span and after the khagne, and the month and day are inferred
stops.campa: At the Sorbonne he reads the history of philosophy under Ferdinand Alquie, Georges Canguilhem, Maurice de Gandillac and Jean Hyppolite, with Gaston Bachelard and Jean Wahl in the same faculty. Claude Lanzmann is a fellow student. Twenty years before him Claude Levi-Strauss took his licence and his agregation in this building. Deleuze finishes a DES thesis in 1947 under Hyppolite and Canguilhem, then passes the agregation in philosophy in 1948, placed eighth. He is twenty-three and has published nothing.
suggested_refs: The 1947 DES thesis directed by Hyppolite and Canguilhem, apparently unpublished

stops.name: Lycee Louis-Thuillier, Amiens: the first post
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1950-1952 by the French record; the English record gives no start year, leaving 1948-1950 unaccounted for. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: His first documented post is at the Lycee Louis-Thuillier in Amiens, teaching philosophy to boys in a cathedral town still clearing its rubble. The French record gives 1950. The English record gives no start year at all, only that the lycee years run until 1957, so the two years after the agregation are unaccounted for by any source checked. He is a provincial schoolmaster in the ordinary rotation of young agreges, and he will be one for seven years.
suggested_refs: Ministry of Education posting records for Deleuze, 1948-1950, the missing two years

stops.name: Lycee Pothier, Orleans: the hole in the life
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1952-1955; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He moves to the Lycee Pothier in Orleans and stays three years. Of the decade opening here he will later say that it was a hole in his life. He shifts between posts, publishes almost nothing after the Hume book, and contracts the respiratory illness that never afterwards lets go of him. Reputations are being made in Paris by men his own age. He is teaching the syllabus to seventeen-year-olds on the Loire, and this goes on until he is thirty-seven.
suggested_refs: Deleuze's own account of the years 1953-1962 as 'a hole in my life', for its original interview context

stops.name: Paris: Empiricism and Subjectivity
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: The first book appears: Empiricism and Subjectivity, on David Hume. It asks how a mind becomes a subject out of nothing but habit and relation. Paris in these years is governed by Hegel and Heidegger; he has gone instead to a Scot who denies that the self is given at all. He is twenty-eight. Nothing else of his will be published for nine years. The book belongs to the genre of the history of philosophy, which carries him for two decades until Guattari arrives and takes it away from him.
suggested_refs: Empiricism and Subjectivity, Presses Universitaires de France, 1953, first edition

stops.name: Lycee Louis-le-Grand: the return as teacher, and the marriage
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1955-1957; the 1956 marriage is attested by year only, and no source names the place. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He returns to Louis-le-Grand, this time on the other side of the desk, closing the loop on the school that trained him ten years earlier. In 1956, at thirty-one, he marries Denise Paule Grandjouan, called Fanny, a translator of D. H. Lawrence into French. No source checked names the arrondissement or the ceremony. Lawrence is in the house from the first year of the marriage. The writers Deleuze returns to are the ones who write bodies and forces rather than subjects and selves.
suggested_refs: Marriage register for Deleuze and Denise Paule Grandjouan, 1956, arrondissement unknown

stops.name: Faculte des Lettres: the first university post
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He is appointed assistant at the Faculte des Lettres of the University of Paris, teaching the history of philosophy in the building where he was a student nine years before. He is thirty-two and the post is junior; he holds it three years. He serves the apparatus of French academic advancement in the correct order, the provincial posts first and the patronage after, with the thesis still unwritten. Later readers will take him for the least institutional philosopher of his generation.
suggested_refs: Faculte des Lettres appointment records, University of Paris, 1957

segments.name: Lyon, and the Friendship with Foucault

stops.name: Quai Claude-Bernard, Lyon: the CNRS fellowship
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1960-1964; month and day defaulted. The birth of Julien is attested to May 1960 with no clinic named
stops.campa: He is named research attache of the CNRS and based at Lyon, on the quai Claude-Bernard, and holds the fellowship four years. It is here that he becomes a friend of Michel Foucault, a friendship that will run through the prisons group, the Vincennes department and two decades of mutual citation. His son Julien is born in Lyon in May of the same year; no clinic is named in any source checked. For four years the state pays him to read, and what he reads is Nietzsche.
suggested_refs: CNRS personnel files for the Lyon research attachment, 1960-1964

stops.name: Lyon: Nietzsche and Philosophy
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Nietzsche and Philosophy appears, and behind it the run that makes him: Kant's Critical Philosophy in 1963, Proust and Signs in 1964, Bergsonism in 1966. He reads the history of philosophy against the grain, taking each thinker as a machine for producing difference rather than a position to be summarised. The Nietzsche book breaks with the dialectic outright, in a France where the dialectic is the common language of the left and Hegel is taught as the horizon of the thinkable.
stops.quote: Evaluations, in essence, are not values but ways of being, modes of existence of those who judge and evaluate.
stops.quote_source: Nietzsche and Philosophy, trans. Hugh Tomlinson (Columbia University Press, 1983 [1962]), p. 1. Cited via Wikiquote; not confirmed against a fetched copy of the Tomlinson translation, so the wording is unverified
suggested_refs: Nietzsche et la philosophie, Presses Universitaires de France, 1962, first edition

stops.name: University of Lyon: charge d'enseignement
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1964-1969; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He is promoted to charge d'enseignement at the University of Lyon and holds the teaching post five years. His daughter Emilie is born the same year. The English record calls the rank a professorship and the French record does not, and the difference matters, because at thirty-nine Deleuze is still well down a ladder that men of his cohort have already climbed. Foucault by now holds the philosophy post at Clermont-Ferrand and is one year from being famous across France.
suggested_refs: University of Lyon faculty rolls, 1964-1969, for the exact grade held

stops.name: Clermont-Ferrand: the appointment the university refuses
stops.date_confidence: attested from the Foucault file for 1966; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Foucault, holding the philosophy post at Clermont-Ferrand, tries to have Deleuze appointed beside him. The university overrules the appointment: it wants neither of them. The refusal is the ordinary business of French faculty politics, and it will be reversed within three years by a state that suddenly needs somewhere to put the philosophers it cannot govern. Foucault does not forget the attempt. He makes it again at Vincennes, from a position where nobody can overrule him.
suggested_refs: Faculty council minutes at Clermont-Ferrand, 1966, on the rejected appointment
sources: michel_foucault.journey.json (stop 'Clermont-Ferrand, the tenured post and the commute')

stops.name: Johns Hopkins, Baltimore: the colloquium neither of them attends
stops.date_confidence: attested for the colloquium from the Barthes file; Deleuze's absence is reconstruction, since no source records an invitation either way
stops.campa: At Johns Hopkins, Roland Barthes, Jacques Lacan and Jacques Derrida convene to explain French thought to America, and structuralism crosses the Atlantic under that name. Foucault does not attend. Neither does Deleuze. That April the Paris press had filed Foucault together with Claude Levi-Strauss, Lacan and Barthes under a label Foucault rejected, and Deleuze is habitually named in the same journalistic cluster in the same months. The Americans are given the wing without two of its members.
suggested_refs: The 1966 Johns Hopkins colloquium programme and its list of invitees
sources: roland_barthes.journey.json (stop 'Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, the structuralism colloquium')
michel_foucault.journey.json (stop 'Paris, Les Mots et les choses sells like hot cakes')

stops.name: The Sorbonne: the two theses
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the defence and publication; month and day unknown and defaulted
stops.campa: He defends his doctorate: Difference and Repetition as the principal thesis, Expressionism in Philosophy: Spinoza as the secondary. The main thesis argues that difference comes before identity and repetition before the general, and everything written afterwards assumes it. The Spinoza book supplies the vocabulary of expression and immanence he will use for the rest of his life. He is forty-three, and the two books arrive in the year the barricades go up in the streets outside.
suggested_refs: The jury report on the 1968 defence of Difference et repetition

stops.name: The Limousin: the lung
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the French record names only the region for the convalescence, not the town. Saint-Leonard-de-Noblat is documented only as the burial place. Month inferred
stops.campa: A pulmonary haemorrhage. He undergoes a thoracoplasty, loses a lung, and goes to convalesce in the Limousin with his wife. The French record names the region and no town; Saint-Leonard-de-Noblat, where his family has ties, is documented only as the place of burial, and the convalescence is pinned here on the strength of that tie alone. The tuberculosis diagnosed this year governs the rest of the life. It sets what he can breathe and how far he will travel, and it is still in the room at the window twenty-seven years on.
suggested_refs: Medical or family records naming the actual Limousin convalescence site, 1968-1969

stops.name: Vincennes: the department Foucault builds
stops.date_confidence: attested from the Foucault file for December 1968; Deleuze's nomination is attested to 1969
stops.campa: Back from Tunis, Foucault is handed the philosophy department of the new experimental university at Vincennes and staffs it with the militant left. He brings Gilles Deleuze in at last, two years after Clermont-Ferrand refused him. The campus goes up in prefabricated blocks in the Bois de Vincennes in January 1969, built to absorb students the state cannot otherwise place. Deleuze is named to a permanent post. The French record says he does not actually arrive for another two years.
suggested_refs: Founding appointment lists of the Vincennes philosophy department, 1968-1969
sources: michel_foucault.journey.json (stop 'Paris, the Sorbonne... Vincennes and the Chair')

stops.name: Paris: the meeting with Felix Guattari
stops.date_confidence: contested; the English accounts place the meeting at Vincennes, the French account in the Limousin during the convalescence. The Paris pin is a placeholder for an undetermined site. Month inferred
stops.campa: He meets Felix Guattari: psychoanalyst, political militant, veteran of the La Borde clinic. The English accounts place the meeting at Vincennes in the aftermath of May; the French account ties it instead to the Limousin convalescence of the same year. The sources do not agree on where two men who will write four books together first sat down. What follows is twenty-two years of collaboration in which neither signature can afterwards be separated out of the text by anyone, including them.
suggested_refs: Correspondence between Deleuze and Guattari from 1969, which would date and place the first meeting

stops.name: Clinique de La Borde, Cour-Cheverny: the clinic
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; no source checked states that Deleuze himself ever visited La Borde. The date is a placeholder for an undocumented association
stops.campa: At Cour-Cheverny, in a chateau in the Loir-et-Cher, Guattari has worked since 1955 in the psychiatric clinic of La Borde, where patients run the kitchen rota and the newspaper, put on plays, and the line between staff and inmate is kept deliberately unstable. La Borde is routinely called the ground of Anti-Oedipus. No source checked states that Deleuze himself ever went there. The association is traditional. The visit is not documented, and this stop records the gap.
suggested_refs: Visitor records or staff memoirs of La Borde naming Deleuze on the premises

stops.name: College de France: the chair that never comes
stops.date_confidence: attested for Foucault's inaugural lecture from the Foucault file; the Deleuzian absence is a documented negative, not an event
stops.campa: Foucault gives his inaugural lecture at the College de France, elected to a chair he has named Histoire des systemes de pensee; Claude Levi-Strauss has held a chair in the same house since 1959. Deleuze never receives one. He remains at Vincennes and then Saint-Denis for the whole of his university career, in the least prestigious philosophy department in France. The absence against this pin is as well documented as any presence. The same year, Foucault reviews his two theses.
stops.quote: one day, perhaps, this century will be called Deleuzian
stops.quote_source: Michel Foucault, quoted in en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilles_Deleuze. The quotation is confirmed; the usual apparatus around it (a 1970 review in Critique titled 'Theatrum Philosophicum', covering both theses) is not confirmed by any source checked this session
suggested_refs: Foucault, 'Theatrum Philosophicum', Critique 282 (1970), to verify the date and venue of the review
sources: michel_foucault.journey.json (stops on the College de France election and inaugural lecture)

stops.name: Vincennes: the weekly seminar
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the French record says he came to Vincennes two years after the campus opened, which puts the first seminars circa 1970-1971 rather than 1969
stops.campa: The weekly seminar begins. It is open to anyone: students, analysts, painters, addicts, foreigners with no French, people who come for the noise. Deleuze talks for two or three hours at a stretch with the tape recorders running, and those recordings become the corpus that transcripts and translations will live off for fifty years. He is not delivering a syllabus. He works the books out in the room, in front of whoever is present, and the room is part of the machinery.
stops.quote: A book is a small cog in a much more complex external machinery.
stops.quote_source: 'I Have Nothing to Admit', interview, trans. Janis Forman, Semiotext(e) 2/3 (1977). Widely cited via Wikiquote; not verified against a fetched copy of the Semiotext(e) issue
suggested_refs: The Vincennes seminar tapes, now the basis of the Purdue Deleuze transcript archive

stops.name: Paris: the Groupe d'Information sur les Prisons
stops.date_confidence: attested for the GIP's declaration in February 1971; Deleuze's participation is reconstruction, since the Foucault file names only Foucault, Vidal-Naquet and Domenach
stops.campa: The Groupe d'Information sur les Prisons is declared from Foucault's own flat. The aim is not to speak for prisoners but to arrange for prisoners to speak. Deleuze is a co-signer and an active participant alongside Foucault, Sartre and Genet, though the Foucault file names only Foucault, Vidal-Naquet and Domenach among the founders. In March of the same year a Buenos Aires songwriter of twenty-one, Luis Alberto Spinetta, walks these streets reading Foucault and Antonin Artaud, and takes both home.
suggested_refs: The founding GIP manifesto of February 1971 and its full list of signatories
sources: michel_foucault.journey.json (stops on the GIP and 'the gates of La Sante')

stops.name: Editions de Minuit, rue Bernard-Palissy: Anti-Oedipus
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 1972; month inferred, day defaulted
stops.campa: Editions de Minuit, at number 7 in the rue Bernard-Palissy, publishes L'Anti-Oedipe, the first volume of Capitalism and Schizophrenia. It opens on the body as a factory, treats desire as production rather than lack, and reads as an assault on psychoanalysis because it is meant as one. The book becomes a bestseller and a scandal at the same time. This is the moment Deleuze stops being a historian of philosophy in the eyes of everyone who is not reading him closely.
stops.quote: It is at work everywhere, functioning smoothly at times, at other times in fits and starts. It breathes, it heats, it eats. It shits and fucks. What a mistake to have ever said the id.
stops.quote_source: Anti-Oedipus: Capitalism and Schizophrenia, with Felix Guattari, trans. Robert Hurley, Mark Seem and Helen R. Lane (University of Minnesota Press, 1983), p. 1, opening line of chapter 1, 'Desiring-Production'. Read directly from the PDF
suggested_refs: L'Anti-Oedipe, Editions de Minuit, 1972, first printing

stops.name: Chateau de Cerisy-la-Salle: Nietzsche aujourd'hui
stops.date_confidence: the colloquium and its 1972 date are attested; Deleuze's own presence is unconfirmed by any source checked. Month inferred, day defaulted
stops.campa: At the chateau of Cerisy-la-Salle in the Manche, the international cultural centre holds a session titled Nietzsche aujourd'hui. The colloquium is confirmed and dated. Deleuze's presence at it is not confirmed by any source checked. Tradition puts him there with the paper Pensee nomade, printed in the 1973 proceedings, which reads Nietzsche as a writer of intensities that no state apparatus can code. This stop is entered on the strength of the publication record and stands or falls with it.
suggested_refs: Nietzsche aujourd'hui?, UGE 10/18, 1973, the printed proceedings with their list of speakers

stops.name: New York: the one journey abroad
stops.date_confidence: the trip is attested for 1975; the city, host and occasion are unknown, and New York is the commonest guess rather than a record. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He goes to the United States, the only trip abroad in a life spent almost entirely inside France. Stanford confirms the journey and names no city, no host and no occasion; New York is marked here as the commonest guess and nothing better. In May of the same year Foucault takes LSD at Zabriskie Point in Death Valley and says afterwards that it altered what he thought about the subject. Two men cross America in one year, and the record of Deleuze's crossing is a single sentence.
suggested_refs: Any American conference programme or invitation naming Deleuze in 1975, which would fix the city
sources: michel_foucault.journey.json (stop 'Death Valley, LSD at Zabriskie Point')

stops.name: Editions de Minuit: A Thousand Plateaus
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Mille Plateaux appears from Minuit, eight years after the first volume. It is built as a book to be entered anywhere: fifteen plateaus, each dated, none requiring the one before it. The rhizome replaces the tree, the map replaces the tracing, and the refrain, the war machine and the body without organs enter the vocabulary of disciplines that will spend forty years borrowing from them. Guattari and Deleuze sign it jointly and neither ever says which sentence is whose.
stops.quote: We're tired of trees. We should stop believing in trees, roots, and radicles.
stops.quote_source: A Thousand Plateaus: Capitalism and Schizophrenia, with Felix Guattari, trans. Brian Massumi (University of Minnesota Press, 1987), Introduction: Rhizome, p. 15. Retrieved from the Massumi text at theanarchistlibrary.org
suggested_refs: Mille Plateaux, Editions de Minuit, 1980, first printing

stops.name: Universite Paris VIII, Saint-Denis: the campus razed
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Vincennes buildings were demolished 27-29 August 1980 and the move took effect at the start of the September term
stops.campa: The state closes the Vincennes campus and razes it between the twenty-seventh and the twenty-ninth of August. The university is moved, against its faculty and against its students, to new buildings in Saint-Denis between the rue de la Liberte, the avenue Lenine and the avenue de Stalingrad. Deleuze carries the seminar to the new site at the start of the September term. The address changes and the room does not: the same recorders, the same unregistered audience, the same hours.
suggested_refs: Photographs of the demolition of the Vincennes campus, 27-29 August 1980

stops.name: Editions de Minuit: Francis Bacon, and the cinema books
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1981, 1983 and 1985 respectively; months and days defaulted
stops.campa: Francis Bacon: The Logic of Sensation appears, on a painter who paints the figure being deformed by forces instead of painting the figure. Then the two cinema volumes: The Movement-Image in 1983, The Time-Image in 1985, a taxonomy of film signs built on Bergson and running to some nine hundred pages across the pair. He is writing on paint and on film while teaching philosophy, and treating both as thought conducted in its own material rather than as illustration of anything.
suggested_refs: Francis Bacon: logique de la sensation, Editions de la Difference, 1981, in its two-volume first edition

stops.name: Pitie-Salpetriere, Paris: the death of Foucault
stops.date_confidence: attested from the Foucault file
stops.campa: Michel Foucault dies at the Pitie-Salpetriere at fifty-seven. Deleuze loses the friend he made in Lyon twenty-four years earlier, the man who tried twice to get him hired and succeeded once. Four years before, Roland Barthes had died in the same hospital after being struck by a laundry van near the Sorbonne. Deleuze will die in Paris eleven years after Foucault. The three endings sit inside a few kilometres of one another, in the hospitals and arrondissements this atlas has already mapped.
suggested_refs: Deleuze's remarks at Foucault's funeral, June 1984
sources: roland_barthes.journey.json (stop 'Pitie-Salpetriere, the death of Roland Barthes')

stops.name: Editions de Minuit: Foucault
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He publishes Foucault, two years after the death. It is not a memorial. It rebuilds the friend's thought as a system of strata, diagrams and folds, in the vocabulary of the man doing the reading rather than the man being read. It is the only book he devotes to a contemporary. Sixteen years earlier Foucault had written that one day, perhaps, this century would be called Deleuzian, and each of the two spends part of his career insisting that the other one is the event.
suggested_refs: Foucault, Editions de Minuit, 1986, first edition

stops.name: Universite Paris VIII: the retirement
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 1987; month inferred from the academic calendar, day defaulted
stops.campa: He retires from Paris VIII at sixty-two, closing the longest institutional chapter of the life. The English record counts eighteen years at Vincennes and Saint-Denis together; if the French account of his late arrival at Vincennes is right, the span is nearer sixteen, and no source resolves the difference. The seminar stops. What survives of it is several hundred hours of tape recorded by people who came for their own reasons and kept the machines running to the end.
suggested_refs: Paris VIII personnel records fixing the exact start and end of Deleuze's tenure

stops.name: Editions de Minuit: The Fold
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Le Pli appears from Minuit: Leibniz read as the philosopher of the fold, the baroque taken as an operation rather than a period, matter folded into matter without end and the soul a room with no windows in it. He is sixty-three and the lungs are worse each year. It is the last solo book of any size he will finish. The queue that carried Deleuze into this atlas names him by this book and by no other, so he arrives here under the sign of the fold rather than the rhizome.
suggested_refs: Le Pli: Leibniz et le baroque, Editions de Minuit, 1988, first edition

stops.name: Paris: L'Abecedaire, filmed with Claire Parnet
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the 1988-1989 recording dates and Boutang's direction were not confirmed by any source fetched. The broadcast date is contested between the French and English records
stops.campa: Over two winters he sits for Claire Parnet, his former student, and talks his way through the alphabet on camera: A for animal, B for drink, G for the left. He says on film that he drank hard for years and then stopped. The condition reported for the filming is that it screen only after his death, and French television broadcasts it in January 1995, ten months before he dies, so the condition as reported cannot be true as stated. Nobody has resolved it. The DVD sells eighty thousand.
suggested_refs: Arte broadcast schedules for L'Abecedaire, to settle the January 1995 date against the posthumous condition

stops.name: Paris: the conversation with Antonio Negri
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the pool gives no date for the conversation itself, only for the collection Negotiations 1972-1990, published in English in 1995. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Antonio Negri, the Italian theorist of autonomia, puts questions to him and the answers are printed as Control and Becoming, collected in Negotiations. Deleuze tells him that the disciplinary societies are giving way to control societies that are no longer exactly disciplinary, and that belief in this world, rather than in another one, is what precipitates the events small enough to slip through. Negri is asking a philosopher of desire what a militant should do. The answer he takes away is an instruction about where to look.
stops.quote: The key thing may be to create vacuoles of noncommunication, circuit breakers, so we can elude control.
stops.quote_source: 'Control and Becoming', conversation with Antonio Negri, in Negotiations 1972-1990, trans. Martin Joughin (Columbia University Press, 1995). Retrieved from the generation-online.org text of the interview
suggested_refs: Pourparlers 1972-1990, Editions de Minuit, 1990, for the French dating of the Negri exchange

stops.name: Editions de Minuit: What Is Philosophy?
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Qu'est-ce que la philosophie? is the last book signed with Guattari. The answer it gives is that philosophy creates concepts, distinct from the functions of science and the affects of art, all three cutting into chaos by different means. It is a book about what the two of them have been doing since 1969, written at the end of it. They have collaborated for twenty-two years, since the year of the barricades and the ruined lung, and this is where the joint signature stops.
suggested_refs: Qu'est-ce que la philosophie?, Editions de Minuit, 1991, first edition

stops.name: Paris: the Postscript on the Societies of Control
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1992 publication in October 59; month and day defaulted. The Negri conversation is undated in the pool and reaches print in Negotiations, 1995
stops.campa: The Postscript on the Societies of Control is published: the disciplinary enclosures Foucault mapped are giving way to modulation, debt and continuous assessment, the mole giving way to the serpent, the individual dissolving into the dividual and the sample. It is four pages long and will be cited more often than most of the books. It names the new figures without proposing a politics to meet them: the corporation that replaces the factory, the perpetual training that replaces the school, the debt that never closes. Foucault has been dead eight years and the argument is still being carried in his direction.
stops.quote: There is no need to fear or hope, but only to look for new weapons.
stops.quote_source: Postscript on the Societies of Control, trans. Martin Joughin, October 59 (1992), section 1, 'Historical'. Verbatim from the full text at theanarchistlibrary.org; the widely circulated 'There's no need' is a Wikiquote rendering
suggested_refs: Post-scriptum sur les societes de controle, in L'Autre journal, 1990, the French first appearance
sources: theanarchistlibrary.org text of the Joughin translation

stops.name: 84 avenue Niel: the last apartment
stops.date_confidence: attested for the address and the final years; the specific year is a placeholder within the period 1990-1995
stops.campa: His last apartment is at 84 avenue Niel, in the 17th arrondissement, the district he was born in. He is tethered to oxygen, and writing has become physical labour. In 1995 he publishes a short text, Immanence: A Life, on the impersonal life that flickers in a dying man between the individual and nothing at all. He has announced a book on Marx, La Grandeur de Marx, the greatness of Marx, and it is not going to be written. The essay on immanence belongs to a larger unfinished project he calls Ensembles and Multiplicities.
suggested_refs: The building at 84 avenue Niel, Paris 17e, unmarked

stops.name: 84 avenue Niel: the window
stops.date_confidence: attested; the French record adds the hour, about half past twelve
stops.campa: At about half past twelve on the fourth of November he throws himself from the window of the apartment on the avenue Niel. He is seventy. Both the English and the French accounts tie the act directly to the respiratory illness that had confined him and had turned breath, then speech, then writing into work. A later reading treats the defenestration as a last act of his own philosophy of immanence; no primary source records him or anyone near him framing it that way.
suggested_refs: Press reports of 4-6 November 1995 in Le Monde and Liberation

stops.name: Saint-Leonard-de-Noblat: the grave
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1995; the exact day of burial is not given by the sources checked, and the day is defaulted
stops.campa: He is buried in the cemetery of Saint-Leonard-de-Noblat, in the Haute-Vienne, a small Limousin town his family was tied to and near which he had convalesced after losing the lung. The exact plot is not given by the sources checked. The English record says simply that he lived and was buried here. The philosopher of Paris, who left France once in seventy years, lies four hours south of it in a town of five thousand people, and no plaque in Paris marks the flat, the seminar rooms or either of the schools.
suggested_refs: The municipal cemetery register of Saint-Leonard-de-Noblat, for the plot

stops.name: Paris: the tributes in Liberation
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1995; the day of publication is not given and is defaulted
stops.campa: Giorgio Agamben, Alain Badiou, Jacques Derrida, Jean-Francois Lyotard, Jean-Luc Nancy and Jean-Pierre Faye publish tributes to him in Liberation within days. They agree on very little else. Roland Barthes had been killed by a laundry van in 1980 and Foucault by an illness the papers would not name in 1984. Deleuze is the one who chose the hour, and a generation that had spent thirty years arguing with each other in print files its copy on the same afternoon, in the same newspaper, about the same man.
suggested_refs: Liberation, November 1995, the tribute pages

stops.name: Universite Paris 8, Saint-Denis: the citations and the absent plaque
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 2007 citation study; month and day defaulted. The absence of any plaque is an argument from silence across the sources checked
stops.campa: By a 2007 citation study he ranks eleventh among the most-cited authors in English-language humanities publishing, between Freud and Kant. The position is built almost entirely after his death and on translations that arrived late: Difference and Repetition into English in 1994, twenty-six years after the French, The Logic of Sense in 1990, Nietzsche and Philosophy in 1983. No plaque, no monument and no room named for him is recorded at any address he used. Two unfinished essays are all the Marx book left.
suggested_refs: The 2007 citation study ranking Deleuze eleventh, cited but not named by the English Wikipedia article
